answer: In June 2012 (thread 'Bibliographic data in CRM / LIDO - authoritative mappings, help urgently requested'), Michael Hopwood (EDItEUR, Linked Heritage project lead) asked the SIG for help mapping ONIX for Books 3.0.1 to LIDO, for integration of commercial book-industry product data into Europeana. The main objection came from Patrick Le Boeuf (BnF, CRM/FRBR Harmonisation Group), who said he was 'totally perplexed' and that mapping ONIX to LIDO was 'simply impossible': ONIX describes abstract, non-unique publications (better suited to MARC/MODS or FRBRoo), while LIDO is designed for unique physical objects, so treating a 'manifestation' as a unique LIDO item, or printed text as an 'inscription', stretches both models' semantics too far; he also questioned why one would map ONIX to LIDO in the first place. Martin Doerr agreed LIDO was 'not intended for such material' and suggested CRM-FRBRoo would fit better, warning that 'abusing an XML schema for another domain... does not help interoperability,' which should instead come via RDF aggregation under CRM/FRBRoo. Regine Stein (LIDO co-chair) took a more moderating middle position: she distinguished the conceptual models (CRM/FRBRoo) from the XML metadata standards (LIDO/ONIX) and reframed Hopwood's work as a legitimate 'schema crosswalk' / analysis exercise to reveal where LIDO's structures match or fall short of book-industry data needs -- explicitly not implying LIDO should actually be used to encode this data -- and argued such analysis could help identify needed sub-property specializations for interoperability. Hopwood himself defended the exercise (in the companion thread 'Bibliographic data in CRM / LIDO', t0630), noting existing ONIX-MARC mappings already treat many class-level properties as inherited by individual items in practice, that LIDO doesn't explicitly prohibit conceptual objects, and listing several Linked Heritage-driven justifications (EC project mandate, enrichment of heritage/commercial data, linked-data trust via identifiers like ISBN/ISTC/ISNI). The thread was forwarded to the FRBR-CRM Harmonization Group and ended without a resolution -- positions ranged from Le Boeuf's 'impossible, and not clear why one would try' to Doerr's 'not intended, do interoperability via RDF instead' to Stein's 'valid as an analytical crosswalk but not as a data-use recommendation' to Hopwood's practical defense based on project requirements.
